chunks: My father (rah) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bazanti from Aban ibn Uthman from Kathir al-Nawwa'i from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, Nuh (peace be upon him) boarded the ark on the first day of Rajab, so he ordered those with him to fast on that day. He said: 'Whoever fasts on that day, the Fire will be distant from him by a year's journey. And whoever fasts for seven days, the seven doors of Hell will be closed for him. And whoever fasts for eight days, the eight doors of Paradise will be opened for him. And whoever fasts for fifteen days, his request will be granted. And whoever increases [in fasting], Allah, the Mighty and Sublime, will increase [his reward] for him.'

key_terms.النِّیرَان: The Hellfire (specifically referring to the seven gates of Hell)
key_terms.الْجَنَّه: Paradise (specifically referring to the eight gates of Paradise)
key_terms.رَجَب: Rajab (the seventh month of the Islamic lunar calendar)
key_terms.مَسِیرَهَ سَنَه: A year's journey (a measure of distance in the afterlife)

ai.seo_question: What are the rewards for fasting on the first of Rajab according to the hadith of Nuh (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: In Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-Amal*, this hadith links the first of Rajab to Prophet Nuh’s embarkation, establishing it as a day of significant merit where fasting serves as a spiritual safeguard against Hellfire. The text details a graduated reward system, promising that fasting for fifteen days grants one’s supplications, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the sanctity of Rajab’s early days and the intercessory power of righteous deeds.
